1	# Data Lineage Trust Platform
2	
3	Backend service for managing datasets, their immutable schema versions and
4	field-level lineage between schema versions. All metadata is persisted in a
5	SQLite database, so data created before a restart remains queryable afterwards.
6	
7	## Requirements
8	
9	- Python 3.12+
10	
11	## Install and test
12	
13	```bash
14	python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
15	python -m pytest
16	```
17	
18	## Start
19	
20	```bash
21	python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
22	```
23	
24	The SQLite database is stored at `data/lineage.db` by default. Override the
25	location with the `DATA_LINEAGE_DB` environment variable.
26	
27	## Public API
28	
29	All endpoints return JSON. Error responses use the stable shape
30	`{"error": "<code>", "detail": "<message>"}` and never expose SQL or stack
31	traces.
32	
33	### Health
34	
35	- `GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}` when the service is ready.
36	
37	### Datasets
38	
39	- `POST /datasets` — create a dataset. Body: `{"name": "orders", "description": "optional"}`.
40	  Returns `201` with `id`, `name`, `description`, `created_at`. Empty name →
41	  `422`; duplicate name → `409`.
42	- `GET /datasets` — list all datasets.
43	
44	### Schema versions (immutable, numbered from 1 per dataset)
45	
46	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions` — create the next schema version. Body:
47	  `{"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": false}]}`.
48	  Field list must be non-empty, field `name`/`type`/`nullable` are required and
49	  field names must be unique within the version. Unknown dataset → `404`;
50	  invalid fields → `422` (nothing is written).
51	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions` — list all versions of a dataset with
52	  their fields.
53	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}` — read one version with its
54	  fields. Unknown dataset/version → `404`.
55	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{base_version}/compatibility/{target_version}` —
56	  read-only breaking-change check of the target version against the base
57	  version, computed fresh from the persisted field definitions on every read
58	  (nothing is written; field order is not a difference). The endpoint takes no
59	  request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version →
60	  `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the version diff. The JSON
61	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
62	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `base_version`, `target_version`,
63	  `breaking_changes` and `breaking_change_count`. A breaking change is exactly
64	  one of: the target removed a base field (`removed`), changed a field's type
65	  (`type_changed`) or tightened a nullable field to not nullable
66	  (`nullable_tightened`); added fields and nullable loosening are not
67	  breaking. Each entry has `field`, `kind`, `before` (base definition) and
68	  `after` (target definition, `null` for a removed field), entries are sorted
69	  by field name ascending and `breaking_change_count` equals the number of
70	  entries. Comparing a version with itself returns an empty list and a zero
71	  count. The verdict is advisory for release decisions only: it runs no
72	  migration or rollback.
73	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{base_version}/compatibility/{target_version}/impact` —
74	  read-only companion of the compatibility check: the same top-level keys
75	  (`base_version`, `target_version`, `breaking_changes`,
76	  `breaking_change_count`) and the same breaking entries, each entry carrying
77	  one extra key `impacted` after `after`. `impacted` lists every field
78	  directly or indirectly downstream of the broken field along the lineage
79	  mappings, starting from the base version's same-named field and — when the
80	  field still exists in the target version — also from the target version's
81	  field. Each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`; the set is
82	  deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate) and is
83	  sorted by dataset, version and field ascending. A field with no downstream
84	  yields an empty list. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
85	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404` with the same
86	  404-before-422 precedence as the compatibility check, and the JSON document
87	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
88	  newline). The read is fully side-effect free: version definitions, lineage
89	  mappings and the impact cache are never written.
90	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/evolution-summary` — read-only whole-dataset
91	  summary of adjacent-version breaking changes and their downstream impact,
92	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version
93	  definitions, lineage mappings and the impact cache are never touched).
94	  Quality and privacy state play no role. The path carries only the dataset
95	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an unknown
96	  dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
97	  compatibility reads. A dataset with fewer than two versions returns `200`
98	  with an empty `pairs` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
99	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
100	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`, `pairs` and `totals`.
101	  `pairs` is ordered by base version number ascending and lists every
102	  adjacent version pair, including pairs without breaking changes; each entry
103	  has exactly `base_version`, `target_version`, `breaking_count`,
104	  `impacted_count` and `impacted_datasets` in that order. `breaking_count` is
105	  the number of breaking entries of the pair, judged exactly as in the
106	  pairwise compatibility impact response (`removed`, `type_changed` or
107	  `nullable_tightened`; several changes of one field collapse into a single
108	  entry). The pair's impacted set is the union of every breaking entry's
109	  downstream fields — same start-field rule as the pairwise impact response,
110	  merged and deduplicated, never containing a start field itself (cycles
111	  terminate) — `impacted_count` is its size and `impacted_datasets` lists the
112	  distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. `totals` has
113	  exactly `pair_count` (the number of pairs), `breaking_count` and
114	  `impacted_count`, each the sum of the per-pair values over the whole
115	  dataset.
116	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/fields/{field}/trajectory` — read-only
117	  cross-version trajectory of one named field of the dataset, computed fresh
118	  on every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions,
119	  lineage mappings and the impact cache are never touched). Only the
120	  persisted version field definitions and lineage mappings are read; quality,
121	  privacy, snapshot and processing-task state play no role. The path carries
122	  the dataset name and the field name; the request takes no body and no query
123	  parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, and a field that does not
124	  appear in any of the dataset's versions → `404`, both with the same
125	  404-before-422 precedence as the evolution summary. A dataset with fewer
126	  than two versions returns `200` with an empty `changes` array, never an
127	  error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
128	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
129	  `field`, `entries` and `changes` in that order. `entries` lists every
130	  schema version of the dataset ordered by version number ascending; each
131	  entry has exactly `version` and `definition`, where `definition` is the
132	  field's persisted definition in that version (`type` and `nullable` only)
133	  or `null` — the key is never omitted — when the field does not exist
134	  there. `changes` lists one entry per adjacent version pair, ordered by
135	  base version ascending; each entry has exactly `base_version`,
136	  `target_version`, `status`, `impacted` and `impacted_datasets` in that
137	  order. `status` reuses the breaking-entry vocabulary of the compatibility
138	  check — `added` (the field appears on the target side), `removed` (it
139	  disappears on the target side), `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened` —
140	  extended with `nullable_loosened` (only the nullability relaxes) and
141	  `unchanged` (both definitions agree, including both absent); a field that
142	  both changes type and tightens nullability collapses into a single
143	  `type_changed` status. `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly
144	  downstream of the tracked field for that pair along the lineage mappings,
145	  with the same start-field rule as the pairwise compatibility impact
146	  response (the base version's same-named field and, when it exists, the
147	  target version's); each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`, the set
148	  is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate),
149	  is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending and is empty when the
150	  field has no downstream. `impacted_datasets` lists the distinct dataset
151	  names appearing in `impacted`, sorted ascending.
152	
153	### Field-level lineage
154	
155	A lineage link maps one field of a target schema version to one field of a
156	schema version in a different (source) dataset.
157	
158	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — register a mapping.
159	  Body names both ends:
160	
161	  ```json
162	  {
163	    "target_dataset": "dm_orders",
164	    "target_version": 1,
165	    "target_field": "id",
166	    "source_dataset": "raw_orders",
167	    "source_version": 1,
168	    "source_field": "order_id"
169	  }
170	  ```
171	
172	  Target must match the path. Source and target datasets must differ and every
173	  referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404` / `422` otherwise).
174	  Submitting the same complete mapping twice returns `409`.
175	- `DELETE /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — remove one
176	  registered mapping. Same address and same body shape as registration: the
177	  six locating fields name the complete mapping to delete and the body target
178	  must match the path. Every locating value readable in the request is
179	  resolved first, so an unknown dataset, version or field is a `404` ahead of
180	  every request-shape error; when all six values name existing resources but
181	  the mapping itself was never registered, the delete is likewise a `404`.
182	  An empty or whitespace body, invalid JSON, a non-object payload, missing or
183	  extra fields, wrongly typed values, blank names, any query parameter, a
184	  mapping whose source and target datasets coincide or whose body target
185	  disagrees with the path are all `422`. No rejection changes the lineage
186	  graph, the impact cache or any other metadata. A registered mapping is
187	  deleted atomically and returns `200` with the removed mapping in the
188	  registration response shape; concurrent deletes of the same mapping succeed
189	  exactly once (the loser gets `404` and changes nothing). The deletion is
190	  visible to every lineage read immediately and survives restarts; the cached
191	  impacts of the mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it
192	  are invalidated exactly as on registration, unrelated entries are kept.
193	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — return every target
194	  field (including fields without sources) together with its source references.
195	  Results are sorted by target field name, then source dataset name, source
196	  version and source field name.
197	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact?field=<field>` —
198	  return the downstream impact of one source field. The path and the `field`
199	  query parameter together name an existing field; the response is
200	  `{"source": {...}, "impacted": [...]}` where `impacted` lists every field
201	  reachable from the source along lineage mappings (direct and indirect), each
202	  entry being `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. Results are deduplicated,
203	  never contain the source itself (cycles terminate) and are sorted by dataset,
204	  version and field ascending. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; a
205	  missing, blank, invalid or repeated `field` parameter → `422` (a repeated
206	  `field` is judged before the field lookup, so it is always a `422`, never a
207	  field `404`).
208	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit` —
209	  read-only consistency audit of the version's impact cache, appended one
210	  segment after the impact query address. The path dataset and version name
211	  the audit scope; every field of that version is checked against its current
212	  cache record and recomputed fresh from the committed lineage graph using
213	  exactly the impact-query semantics (downstream fields merged and
214	  deduplicated, the start field excluded, cycles terminating). Each entry is
215	  `{"field", "status"}` with `cached` (the stored record equals the
216	  recomputed result), `missing` (no cache record because the field's impact
217	  was never queried — a normal state, not an error) or `mismatch` (the stored
218	  record differs). Entries are sorted by field name ascending and the sort
219	  does not depend on database order. The JSON document is deterministic
220	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with
221	  top-level keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order;
222	  `counts` gives `cached_count`, `missing_count` and `mismatch_count`, each
223	  equal to the number of entries with that status. The audit is computed on
224	  every read and never writes: no cache record is inserted, invalidated or
225	  repaired, so impact queries, impact paths and source paths behave exactly
226	  as before. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters; any
227	  body bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, and an
228	  unknown dataset or version → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over
229	  `422` as in the impact query.
230	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit/repair`
231	  — controlled repair of the version's impact cache, appended one segment
232	  after the read-only audit address and accepting POST only. Every field of
233	  the version is recomputed against the committed lineage graph with the
234	  exact impact-query semantics: a field without a cache record gets one
235	  (`created`), a stored record that disagrees is rewritten (`updated`) and a
236	  matching record is left untouched (`unchanged`). Entries are sorted by
237	  field name ascending and the JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
238	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level
239	  keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order; each
240	  entry has exactly `field` and `action`, and `counts` gives
241	  `created_count`, `updated_count` and `unchanged_count`. Written records
242	  are ordinary cache rows visible immediately to impact queries and
243	  surviving restarts; a subsequent audit reports every field as `cached`.
244	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters — any body
245	  bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, an unknown
246	  dataset or version → `404` (with `404` taking precedence as in the audit),
247	  and concurrent repairs of the same version have a single winner, the
248	  loser receiving `409` and changing nothing. Every rejection writes
249	  nothing; lineage registrations and deletions, impact queries, path
250	  explanations, source-path reads and the read-only audit are unaffected.
251	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact-paths?field=<field>` —
252	  read-only shortest-path explanation of the same impact, computed fresh on
253	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions, lineage
254	  mappings and the impact cache are never touched). The path and the `field`
255	  query parameter together name an existing field. The JSON document is
256	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
257	  newline) with top-level keys `source`, `impacts`, `direct_count` and
258	  `indirect_count` in that order; `source` is the start field reference
259	  (`{"dataset", "version", "field"}`). Each `impacts` entry has exactly the
260	  location keys `dataset`, `version`, `field`, then `path` and `path_length`;
261	  entries are deduplicated, never contain the source and are sorted by dataset,
262	  version and field ascending. `path` is the shortest node sequence from the
263	  source to the field, including both ends, and each node has the same
264	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}` shape; `path_length` is the number of
265	  edges on the path (`1` for a direct downstream field, increasing for
266	  indirect ones). Among several shortest paths, the lexicographically smallest
267	  node sequence (compared by dataset, version and field) is chosen; cycles
268	  terminate. `direct_count` counts fields at distance 1 and `indirect_count`
269	  the fields farther away, and a field with no downstream returns an empty
270	  `impacts` array and both counts zero, never an error. The endpoint takes no
271	  request body and no query parameter other than `field` (a missing, blank or
272	  repeated `field` is likewise a `422`); unknown dataset/version/field →
273	  `404`, with `404` taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated
274	  `field` is judged before the field lookup and is therefore always a `422`.
275	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/source-paths?field=<field>` —
276	  read-only upstream companion of the lineage impact query, computed fresh on
277	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions, lineage
278	  mappings and the impact cache are never touched). The path and the `field`
279	  query parameter together name an existing field; the `field` value is
280	  matched literally (never trimmed), so a whitespace-padded name that matches
281	  no stored field is a `404`. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
282	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys
283	  `source`, `origins`, `direct_count`, `indirect_count` and
284	  `source_dataset_count` in that order; `source` is the start field reference
285	  (`{"dataset", "version", "field"}`). Each `origins` entry has exactly the
286	  location keys `dataset`, `version`, `field`, then `path` and `path_length`;
287	  entries are deduplicated, never contain the start field and are sorted by
288	  dataset, version and field ascending. An origin is a field whose mapping
289	  points (directly or transitively) at the start field. `path` is the
290	  shortest node sequence walking from the start field up to the origin,
291	  including both ends, and each node has the same
292	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}` shape; `path_length` is the number of
293	  edges on the path (`1` for a direct source, increasing for indirect ones).
294	  Among several shortest paths, the lexicographically smallest node sequence
295	  (compared by dataset, version and field) is chosen; cycles terminate.
296	  `direct_count` counts origins at distance 1, `indirect_count` the origins
297	  farther away and `source_dataset_count` the distinct dataset names among
298	  all origins; a field with no sources returns an empty `origins` array and
299	  all counts zero, never an error. The endpoint takes no request body and no
300	  query parameter other than `field` (a missing, blank or repeated `field` is
301	  likewise a `422`); unknown dataset/version/field → `404`, with `404`
302	  taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated `field` is judged
303	  before the field lookup and is therefore always a `422`.
304	
305	  Impact results are cached persistently (they survive restarts) and every
306	  read reflects the currently committed lineage graph: creating a schema
307	  version invalidates the cache entries related to that dataset, and creating
308	  or deleting a lineage mapping invalidates the cached impacts of the
309	  mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it. Unrelated
310	  cache entries are preserved.

312	### Quality rules
313	
314	Quality rules validate rows against a schema version. Rules are version-scoped
315	and persisted (including their enabled state) across restarts.
316	
317	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — create a rule.
318	  Body: `{"name": "id required", "kind": "not_null", "params": {...}}`. Returns
319	  `201` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `params`, `enabled`, `created_at`; `enabled`
320	  defaults to `true`. Rule names must be unique within a version (`409` on
321	  conflict). Referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404`); other invalid
322	  input returns `422` and nothing is written. Supported kinds:
323	  - `not_null` — params `{"field": "<existing field>"}`.
324	  - `numeric_range` — params `{"field": "<existing field>", "min": <finite
325	    number>, "max": <finite number>}` with `min <= max`.
326	  - `unique` — params `{"fields": ["<existing field>", ...]}`: a non-empty list
327	    of distinct, existing field names.
328	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — list rules
329	  sorted by `id` ascending.
330	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/{rule_id}` —
331	  enable or disable a rule. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
332	  the updated rule. Unknown rule/dataset/version → `404`.
333	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluate` —
334	  evaluate rows. Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}`. Only enabled rules run.
335	  Returns `{"dataset", "version", "results"}` with results sorted by `rule_id`;
336	  each result has `rule_id`, `name`, `passed` and `violations` (0-based row
337	  indices in ascending order).
338	  - `not_null` fails on missing or `null` values.
339	  - `numeric_range` fails on missing, `null`, non-numeric, boolean or
340	    out-of-range values (boundaries included).
341	  - `unique` compares the tuple of `fields` values per row; a missing field
342	    counts as `null`, and every row taking part in a duplicate group is a
343	    violation.
344	  - With an empty `rows` list every rule passes.
345	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations` —
346	  list the persisted evaluation history of the version, ordered by `sequence`
347	  (occurrence order). Every successful evaluation appends one immutable
348	  summary (`sequence`, `dataset`, `version`, `row_count`,
349	  `violation_row_count` — the number of distinct submitted rows violating at
350	  least one rule — `results` and `created_at`); rejected or failed
351	  evaluations leave no record, and an empty `rows` submission is recorded
352	  with zero violations. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
353	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
354	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff`
355	  — read-only diff between the two most recent recorded evaluations
356	  (`from_sequence` → `to_sequence`). `added_violation_rows` /
357	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
358	  stopped violating any rule, and each entry of `rules` carries the rule's
359	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
360	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
361	  `violation_count_delta` (negative, zero or positive). A rule missing from
362	  one side (disabled or created between the two evaluations) has a `null`
363	  side and `null` row-level diff fields. With fewer than two recorded
364	  evaluations the response is an explicit empty result (null sequences,
365	  empty lists), not an error. Same `404`/`422` rules as the history
366	  endpoint; nothing is written.
367	
368	### Quality anomaly detection
369	
370	Anomaly detection runs over the persisted evaluation history of a schema
371	version. A version carries at most one detection config; scans append
372	immutable anomaly records that persist across restarts.
373	
374	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
375	  — register the version's detection config. The body contains exactly three
376	  integers: `consecutive_worsening_steps` (at least `2`),
377	  `violation_row_limit` and `rule_violation_limit` (both non-negative).
378	  Returns `201` with the config (`id`, `dataset`, `version`, the three
379	  thresholds, `created_at`). A second config for the same version returns
380	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing, extra, non-integer or
381	  out-of-range fields → `422` and nothing is written.
382	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
383	  — return the registered config (`404` when none exists). The endpoint takes
384	  no request body and no query parameters (`422`).
385	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/scan`
386	  — run one detection pass over the persisted evaluation history and return
387	  the anomaly records this scan newly added (ordered by `id`); they are
388	  persisted in the same transaction. Scanning without a registered config
389	  returns `409`; an empty history is a successful scan that writes nothing.
390	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`). Each
391	  record has `id`, `kind`, `sequence` (the history sequence it points to),
392	  `rule_id`, `violation_count` and `created_at`; `kind` is one of:
393	  - `row_limit` — the evaluation's `violation_row_count` exceeds
394	    `violation_row_limit` (`rule_id` is `null`).
395	  - `rule_limit` — one rule's violation count in the evaluation exceeds
396	    `rule_violation_limit`; `rule_id` carries the rule's id.
397	  - `trend` — the violation row counts of adjacent evaluations strictly
398	    increase and the consecutive increase count at the tail of the history
399	    reaches `consecutive_worsening_steps`; the record points to the final
400	    evaluation of the increasing sequence (`rule_id` is `null`). A shorter
401	    run or any decline produces no trend record.
402	
403	  A record with the same kind, history sequence and rule id is never
404	  duplicated: repeated scans only persist and return newly appearing
405	  anomalies, and concurrent scans store each anomaly exactly once with
406	  contiguous ids.
407	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/anomalies`
408	  — list every anomaly record of the version sorted by `id` ascending (empty
409	  when there are none, never an error). Same `404`/`422` rules as the scan
410	  endpoint; nothing is written.
411	
412	### Quality gate
413	
414	The quality gate is the release-readiness verdict of a schema version. It is
415	computed fresh from the persisted records on every read — nothing is cached,
416	re-run or written, and the rule definitions are never consulted (violations
417	recorded for rules since disabled still count).
418	
419	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate` — return the
420	  verdict as a deterministic JSON document (fixed key order, compact
421	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
422	  `{"dataset", "version", "verdict", "reasons", "counts"}`.
423	  - `verdict` is one of:
424	    - `pass` — the latest recorded evaluation passed every rule and no
425	      anomaly record exists; a zero-violation evaluation left by an empty
426	      `rows` submission is a valid basis.
427	    - `undetermined` — no evaluation was ever recorded; `reasons` is empty
428	      and the read succeeds (never an error).
429	    - `fail` — the latest recorded evaluation still has violating rows, or
430	      the version carries any anomaly record.
431	  - `reasons` lists every factor that lowers the verdict, sorted by `kind`,
432	    `sequence` and `rule_id` (null ids first), all ascending. Each reason has
433	    `kind`, `sequence`, `rule_id` and `violation_count` (a missing rule id is
434	    `null`, never omitted). Every rule with violations in the latest
435	    evaluation contributes one `violation` reason with its violation row
436	    count; every persisted anomaly record contributes one reason of its own
437	    kind (`row_limit`, `rule_limit` or `trend`). A rule that appears in both
438	    yields two reasons — they are never merged or deduplicated.
439	  - `counts` reports how many persisted records the verdict examined:
440	    `evaluations`, `anomalies` and `reasons` (the length of the reason list).
441	  - The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters: any body
442	    bytes — including whitespace-only ones — or any query parameter are a
443	    `422`, checked after the path dataset/version resolves (`404` first).
444	    Nothing is written on any rejection.
445	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate/at?timestamp=...`
446	  — the same verdict as it stood at a requested instant. `timestamp` must be
447	  a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time; only evaluations and anomaly records
448	  written at or before it count, and the latest evaluation of that window is
449	  the one with the highest sequence inside it. The response is the same
450	  deterministic document as the bare gate (`dataset`, `version`, `verdict`,
451	  `reasons`, `counts`, one trailing newline), with the counts covering only
452	  the records inside the window. A window without any evaluation is
453	  `undetermined` with an empty reason list — a normal response, never an
454	  error. The endpoint accepts GET only and is strictly read-only. The path
455	  dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body bytes
456	  (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
457	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
458	  writes nothing.

460	### Privacy policies
461	
462	Privacy policies attach a sensitivity classification and masking strategy to a
463	single field of a schema version, enabling role-based de-identification of row
464	data. Policies (including their enabled state) are persisted across restarts.
465	
466	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — register a
467	  policy. Body:
468	  `{"field": "email", "classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles": ["analyst"]}`.
469	  `field` must name an existing field of the version; `classification` is a
470	  non-empty string; `masking` is `redact` or `partial`; `allowed_roles` is an
471	  array of distinct, non-empty role names and may be empty. Returns `201` with
472	  the submitted fields plus `id`, `enabled` (defaults to `true`) and
473	  `created_at`. Registering two policies for the same field within one version
474	  returns `409`. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; other invalid input →
475	  `422` and nothing is written.
476	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — list policies
477	  sorted by `id` ascending.
478	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
479	  enable or disable a policy. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
480	  the updated policy. Unknown policy/dataset/version → `404`.
481	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
482	  revise a policy. Body carries exactly the three adjustable fields:
483	  `{"classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles":
484	  ["analyst"]}`, using the same value rules as registration — a non-empty
485	  `classification` after trimming, `masking` of `redact` or `partial`, and an
486	  `allowed_roles` array of distinct, non-empty-after-trimming role names that
487	  may be empty. The three fields are replaced together from one whole
488	  submission. The revision never changes the policy id, the field it belongs
489	  to, its `enabled` state or its `created_at`; it writes only the policy
490	  itself — no policy is created, no identification record is touched and no
491	  masking suggestion is registered. Returns `200` with the updated policy in
492	  the same shape as the policy read, and the revision survives restarts. The
493	  next privacy view read (and every later masked read) judges each value by
494	  the revised classification, masking and allowed roles. Already-written
495	  masking-hit records, access records and cleanup requests are unaffected —
496	  their contents and ordering stay as written; the grouping of the summary,
497	  diff and reconciliation responses keeps the same counting rules, while the
498	  policy classification and masking reported on trend rows (and the policy
499	  entries of the coverage check and compliance export) reflect the current
500	  values. Advisory masking suggestions are unaffected. Unknown
501	  dataset/version/policy → `404`, judged before every request-shape check;
502	  missing or extra fields, a blank `classification`, an illegal `masking`
503	  value, duplicate or blank `allowed_roles` entries, an empty or
504	  whitespace-only body, malformed JSON, a non-object payload or any query
505	  parameter → `422` and nothing is written. Concurrent revisions of the same
506	  policy have exactly one winner; the loser receives `409` and changes no
507	  field.
508	
509	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view` — return a
510	  role-scoped, order-preserving copy of submitted rows. Body:
511	  `{"role": "guest", "rows": [{...}, ...]}` with a non-empty `role` and a list
512	  of row objects. Response: `{"dataset", "version", "rows"}`. Only enabled
513	  policies whose field appears in a row mask the value when `role` is not in
514	  `allowed_roles`:
515	  - `redact` replaces every non-`null` value with `"***"`.
516	  - `partial` keeps the first character and last two characters of strings
517	    longer than 4 characters (e.g. `"alice@example.com"` → `"aom"`); every other
518	    non-`null` value (short strings, numbers, booleans, …) is replaced with
519	    `"***"`.
520	  - `null` values and fields without a policy are returned unchanged; rows
521	    missing a covered field are left without it.
522	
523	  Every successful view also appends one audit record per value it actually
524	  masked (the same field masked in several rows yields one record per masked
525	  value; a role in `allowed_roles`, a `null` value, an uncovered field or a
526	  disabled policy never hits); the records are persisted per version and are
527	  append-only.
528	
529	  Every successful view additionally appends exactly one access record,
530	  whether or not it masked any value (an empty `rows` submission is recorded
531	  too). Rejected or failed views leave neither kind of record.
532	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/access-records`
533	  — list every access record of the version, ordered by `sequence` ascending
534	  (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has `sequence`,
535	  `role`, `row_count` (the number of submitted rows), `masked_count` (the
536	  number of masking-hit records the same view wrote, so the two logs
537	  cross-check) and `created_at`. The endpoint takes no request body and no
538	  query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is
539	  written.
540	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records`
541	  — list every masking-hit record of the version, ordered by `sequence`
542	  ascending (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has
543	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`. The
544	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
545	  dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is written.
546	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/search`
547	  — read-only filtered retrieval of the same masking-hit records. The
548	  response is the same record collection as the full list (each record has
549	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`),
550	  sorted by `sequence` ascending; a filter that matches nothing returns an
551	  empty array, never an error. All filters are optional query parameters and
552	  combine with AND:
553	  - `role` — exact match against the requesting role recorded on the hit,
554	    case-insensitive (no substring or other fuzzy matching).
555	  - `field` — exact match against the hit field name, case-insensitive.
556	  - `start` / `end` — closed write-time interval: a record matches when its
557	    `created_at` is between the bounds inclusive. Each bound is a
558	    timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`); either bound may be
559	    given alone. `start` later than `end` → `422`.
560	
561	  The endpoint takes no request body; an unparseable or timezone-less
562	  `start`/`end`, or any query parameter other than `role`, `field`, `start`
563	  and `end`, → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
564	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list. It is strictly read-only:
565	  no record is written, modified or deleted and the summary/diff responses
566	  are unaffected.
567	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/summary`
568	  — read-only compliance summary computed fresh from the persisted records on
569	  every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted). Response:
570	  `{"dataset", "version", "groups"}`; `groups` is an empty array when the
571	  version has no records. Each group merges records with the same `field`,
572	  `policy_id`, `role` and `masking` (different roles or masking modes stay
573	  separate) and lists `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking`, `hit_count`
574	  (one record counts as one hit), `first_hit_at` and `last_hit_at` (the
575	  earliest and latest record `created_at` in the group). Groups sort by
576	  `field`, then `policy_id`, `role` and `masking`, all ascending. The
577	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
578	  dataset/version → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
579	  record list.
580	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/trend`
581	  — read-only hit trend aggregated by privacy policy, computed fresh from the
582	  persisted records on every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted).
583	  Hits of the same policy merge across roles (a disabled policy's historical
584	  hits still count). Response: `{"dataset", "version", "policies", "totals"}`;
585	  `policies` is an empty array when the version has no records. Each policy
586	  row carries `policy_id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `total_hits`
587	  and `days`; policies sort by `policy_id` ascending. `days` lists only UTC
588	  calendar days with hits (a write time with a non-zero offset buckets by its
589	  UTC day), sorted ascending with no zero-filled gaps; each entry has `day`
590	  (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `hit_count` (one record counts once), `hit_count_delta`
591	  (difference from the previous listed day, `null` on the first) and `trend`
592	  (`up`/`down`/`flat`, or `none` on the first day). `totals` gives
593	  `total_hits` (the sum of the row totals), `policy_count` (policies with
594	  hits) and `day_count` (distinct hit days over the whole version, the
595	  per-policy day union). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
596	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
597	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list.
598	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests`
599	  — open a two-stage retention cleanup request for the version's masking-hit
600	  records. Body contains exactly `reason` and `before`:
601	  `{"reason": "legal hold expired", "before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`.
602	  `reason` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace;
603	  `before` must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone (offset or `Z`),
604	  and a record belongs to the target set only when its hit write time is
605	  strictly earlier than that instant. Creating a request only returns a
606	  preview — no hit record is deleted or modified, and the record list,
607	  search, summary, diff, reconcile and trend responses stay unchanged.
608	  Returns `201` with `id`, `reason` (trimmed), `before` (echoed as
609	  submitted), `status` (`pending`), `created_at` and a `preview` block:
610	  `hit_count` (the number of records that would be cleaned up),
611	  `first_hit_at` / `last_hit_at` (the earliest and latest hit times in the
612	  target set, `null` when the set is empty) and `fields` (the distinct field
613	  names involved, sorted ascending; `[]` when empty). The target set is
614	  fixed at creation time: masking-hit records written afterwards never enter
615	  the request even when they precede the cutoff by clock time. At most one
616	  pending request may exist per version; creating another while one is open
617	  returns `409` and writes nothing (confirmed requests never block a new
618	  one). Unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing/non-string/blank `reason`,
619	  missing/unparseable/timezone-less `before`, an extra body field, a
620	  non-JSON/non-object body or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
621	  written, with 404 taking precedence.
622	- `GET .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests` — list the
623	  version's cleanup requests sorted by request `id` ascending (empty when
624	  there are none). Confirmed requests stay listed and requests survive
625	  process restarts. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
626	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
627	- `POST .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests/{request_id}/confirm`
628	  — confirm a request with an empty request body and no query parameters.
629	  Confirmation atomically deletes exactly the target set frozen at creation
630	  and sets `status` to `confirmed`; the response is the request plus
631	  `confirmed_at` and `deleted_count` (the number of records actually
632	  deleted, possibly zero). Confirming an already-confirmed request returns
633	  `409` and never changes data again; concurrent confirmations have exactly
634	  one winner (the others get `409`) and can never leave the records half
635	  deleted. After a cleanup the surviving hit records keep their original
636	  `sequence` numbers and later hits continue the existing increasing run
637	  without reusing cleaned numbers; the record list and search return only
638	  surviving records, and summary, trend, diff and reconcile recompute from
639	  them. Access records are not cleaned up and the processing-task audit
640	  chain remains immutable. A request body or query parameter on the confirm
641	  endpoint → `422`; unknown dataset/version/request → `404` (precedence
642	  matches the hit-record reads), and confirming a confirmed request →
643	  `409`.
644	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-compliance-export` — read-only
645	  cross-version export of the dataset's whole privacy compliance state,
646	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
647	  deleted, and no hit record, access record or cleanup request is touched).
648	  The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no
649	  query parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same
650	  404-before-422 precedence as the hit-record reads. A dataset without
651	  schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero
652	  totals, never an error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
653	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
654	
655	  ```json
656	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"policies":[...],"hit_count":0,"masked_count":1,"view_count":2,"cleanup_requests":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
657	  ```
658	
659	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
660	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
661	  has exactly `version`, `policies`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
662	  `view_count`, `cleanup_requests` in that order. `policies` lists the
663	  version's registered policies ordered by policy id; each policy has `id`,
664	  `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `allowed_roles` and `enabled`.
665	  `cleanup_requests` lists the version's cleanup requests ordered by request
666	  id (both pending and confirmed are retained); each has `id`, `reason`,
667	  `status` and `created_at`. `hit_count` is the number of masking-hit
668	  records currently stored for the version, `masked_count` is the sum of the
669	  access records' masked-value counts and `view_count` is the number of
670	  access records; all three reflect the records surviving a confirmed
671	  cleanup. `totals` has exactly `policy_count`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
672	  `view_count` and `cleanup_request_count`, each the sum of the per-version
673	  values over the whole dataset.
674	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-policy-coverage` — read-only cross-version
675	  check of the dataset's privacy policy coverage, computed fresh on every
676	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no policy
677	  or identification record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
678	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an
679	  unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
680	  compliance export. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
681	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
682	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
683	  one trailing newline):
684	
685	  ```json
686	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[...],"candidates":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
687	  ```
688	
689	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
690	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
691	  has exactly `version`, `fields`, `candidates` in that order. `fields`
692	  lists every field of the version ordered by field name; each entry has
693	  `field`, `coverage`, `classification`, `masking` and `enabled`, where
694	  `coverage` is `enabled` (an enabled policy is registered), `disabled` (a
695	  policy is registered but disabled) or `unregistered` (no policy), and the
696	  last three keys report the registered policy's classification, masking and
697	  enabled state (all `null` when no policy is registered). `candidates`
698	  lists the advisory suggestions for fields that were identified with at
699	  least one name or sample hit but carry no privacy policy yet, ordered by
700	  identification record id ascending; each candidate has exactly `field`,
701	  `classification` and `masking`, and an identified field whose name and
702	  samples both missed does not appear. The candidates are a compliance
703	  self-check reference only: they never register a policy and never rewrite
704	  an identification record. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
705	  `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count`, `unregistered_count`
706	  and `candidate_count`, each the sum of the per-version values over the
707	  whole dataset.
708	
709	### Sensitive-field identification
710	
711	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
712	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
713	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
714	stable ids) persist across restarts.
715	
716	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
717	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
718	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
719	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
720	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
721	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
722	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
723	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
724	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
725	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
726	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
727	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
728	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
729	
730	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
731	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
732	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
733	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
734	
735	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
736	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
737	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
738	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
739	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
740	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
741	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
742	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
743	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
744	    matching is sufficient.
745	
746	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
747	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
748	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
749	
750	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
751	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
752	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
753	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
754	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
755	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
756	
757	#### Masking strategy suggestions
758	
759	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
760	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
761	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
762	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
763	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
764	  empty list rather than an error.
765	
766	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
767	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
768	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
769	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
770	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
771	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
772	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
773	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
774	
775	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
776	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
777	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
778	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
779	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
780	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
781	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
782	
783	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
784	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
785	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
786	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
787	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
788	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
789	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
790	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
791	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
792	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
793	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
794	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
795	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
796	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
797	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
798	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
799	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
800	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
801	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
802	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
803	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
804	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
805	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
806	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.

808	### Row snapshots
809	
810	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
811	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
812	
813	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
814	  Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}` where `rows` must be an array of JSON objects
815	  (it may be empty). The JSON values and the order of rows/object keys are deep
816	  copied verbatim. Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
817	  `created_at` and `row_count` (no rows). Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
818	  malformed or non-object rows → `422` and nothing is written.
819	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — list snapshot
820	  metadata sorted by `id` ascending (no `rows`).
821	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` — return
822	  the metadata together with the saved `rows`. Unknown dataset/version/snapshot
823	  → `404`.
824	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at?timestamp=<ISO-8601>` —
825	  return the most recent snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
826	  `timestamp`, including its rows. The timestamp must be a timezone-aware
827	  ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`): missing, invalid or
828	  timezone-less values return `422`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; when no
829	  snapshot exists at or before the timestamp the response is `404`.
830	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/diff?from=<ISO-8601>&to=<ISO-8601>`
831	  — read-only time-travel row diff, appended one segment after the bare-row
832	  time lookup and accepting GET only. Each of `from` (the baseline) and `to`
833	  (the target) must be a timezone-aware ISO-8601 date-time; each side
834	  independently selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later
835	  than its own timestamp (the same selection as the bare-row lookup), so the
836	  two times may resolve to the same snapshot and a `to` earlier than `from` is
837	  valid — the two snapshots are simply compared in their named order. The
838	  comparison reads snapshots and rows and writes nothing. The JSON document
839	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
840	  newline) with top-level keys `from_timestamp`, `to_timestamp`,
841	  `from_snapshot_id`, `to_snapshot_id`, `added`, `removed`, `fields_added`
842	  and `fields_removed` in that order; the timestamps echo the submitted query
843	  values. `added` and `removed` use the exact comparison semantics of the
844	  snapshot-id diff (JSON-object multisets, key order irrelevant, array order
845	  and value types significant, duplicates counted; entries
846	  `{"row", "count"}` sorted by canonical row text). `fields_added` and
847	  `fields_removed` compare the top-level field names appearing on the
848	  snapshots' row objects: names only on the target side are added, names only
849	  on the baseline side are removed, names on both enter neither set, and each
850	  list sorts by field name ascending. When both times select the same
851	  snapshot all four collections are empty and the request succeeds. Unknown
852	  dataset/version → `404`, checked before every request-shape check; a missing,
853	  blank, repeated, unparseable or timezone-less `from`/`to`, an extra query
854	  parameter or any request body bytes (whitespace-only included) → `422`; a
855	  side with no snapshot at or before its timestamp → `404` and nothing is
856	  written.
857	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/diff/masked` —
858	  role-masked time-travel row diff, appended one segment after the bare-row
859	  time diff and accepting POST only. The body contains exactly `role`,
860	  `from` and `to`: `{"role": "guest", "from": "<ISO-8601>", "to":
861	  "<ISO-8601>"}`; `role` must be non-empty after trimming and each time must
862	  be a timezone-aware ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`). Each side
863	  independently selects the newest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later
864	  than its own timestamp, with exactly the same selection as the bare-row
865	  time lookup. Added and removed entries are first judged and counted from
866	  the raw, unmasked rows with the bare-row diff's JSON-object multiset
867	  semantics (key order irrelevant, array order and value types significant,
868	  duplicates counted): a row appearing several times stays one entry with
869	  its multiplicity, and masking only rewrites the entry's row data — entries
870	  are never merged or split. Entries sort by the canonical (key-sorted) JSON
871	  text of the raw row, so the output order is unaffected by masking. Each
872	  emitted row is then masked exactly as the row-submission privacy view masks
873	  it, applying only the version's currently enabled policies
874	  (`redact`/`partial` semantics, `allowed_roles`, nulls and uncovered fields
875	  behave identically). The response is the same deterministic document as
876	  the bare-row time diff (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
877	  trailing newline) with the same keys in the same order: `from_timestamp`,
878	  `to_timestamp`, `from_snapshot_id`, `to_snapshot_id`, `added`, `removed`,
879	  `fields_added` and `fields_removed`; the timestamps echo the submitted
880	  body values and the field-name sets carry no values, so masking can never
881	  change them. Every successful read appends one masking-hit record per
882	  value it actually masks, counted per occurrence across both snapshots'
883	  diff entries (an entry of count `n` whose covered value is masked yields
884	  `n` hit records; added-side entries first, then removed-side, each side in
885	  canonical row order), structurally identical to the regular view's hit
886	  records and continuing the same per-version sequence run, plus exactly one
887	  access record whose `row_count` is the total number of rows expanded from
888	  both sides' entries and whose `masked_count` equals the number of hit
889	  records the read wrote. The records enter all existing masking-hit/access
890	  reads, filters, summaries, diffs, reconciliation, trends and cleanup
891	  previews; records of one read share a write timestamp, sequences stay
892	  continuous across processes, and a write obstruction never fails the read.
893	  The read never modifies snapshots, rows, policies or identification
894	  records. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; each side with a usable
895	  timestamp is resolved independently, so a side with no snapshot at or
896	  before its timestamp is likewise `404` and precedes every shape check
897	  (including a missing or invalid timestamp on the other side); a missing or
898	  wrong-typed `role`/`from`/`to`, a role blank after trimming, an
899	  unparseable or timezone-less time, an extra body field, an empty,
900	  whitespace-only or non-JSON body, a non-object body and any query
901	  parameter are `422` and write nothing.
902	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/masked-view` —
903	  role-masked time travel, appended one segment after the bare-row time
904	  lookup and accepting POST only. The body contains exactly `role` and
905	  `timestamp`: `{"role": "guest", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`; the
906	  service selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
907	  `timestamp` (the same selection as the bare-row lookup). On success it
908	  returns `{"dataset", "version", "snapshot_id", "created_at", "rows"}`; the
909	  `rows` are an order-preserving copy of the snapshot's rows masked exactly
910	  as the row-submission privacy view masks them, applying only the version's
911	  currently enabled policies (`redact`/`partial` semantics, `allowed_roles`,
912	  nulls and uncovered fields behave identically). Every successful read
913	  appends one masking-hit record per value actually masked, structurally
914	  identical to the regular view's hit records and continuing the same
915	  per-version sequence run, plus exactly one access record whose
916	  `row_count` is the snapshot's row count and whose `masked_count` equals
917	  the number of hit records written by the read. An empty snapshot, an
918	  allowed role, all-null values and a version without policies all succeed
919	  and leave only the access record. The records enter all existing
920	  masking-hit/access reads, filters, summaries, diffs, reconciliation,
921	  trends and cleanup previews; records of one read share a write timestamp,
922	  sequences stay continuous across processes, and a write obstruction never
923	  fails the read. The read never modifies or deletes the snapshot or its
924	  rows and never changes policies or identification records. Unknown
925	  dataset/version → `404`, and no snapshot existing at or before the
926	  timestamp is likewise `404`, both checked before every shape check (the
927	  latter whenever the body carries a usable timestamp); a missing or
928	  wrong-typed `role`/`timestamp`, a role blank after trimming, an
929	  unparseable or timezone-less timestamp, an extra body field, an empty,
930	  whitespace-only or non-JSON body, a non-object body and any query
931	  parameter are `422` and write nothing.
932	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/diff/{other_snapshot_id}` —
933	  compare two snapshots as JSON-object multisets. Object key order does not
934	  affect equality, while array order and JSON value types do (e.g. `1`, `1.0`,
935	  `"1"` and `true` are all distinct), and duplicate rows are counted. Both
936	  snapshots must belong to the dataset and version named in the path, otherwise
937	  `422`; unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404`. The response is
938	  `{"from_snapshot_id", "to_snapshot_id", "added", "removed"}`; `added` lists
939	  rows present more often (or only) in the `to` snapshot and `removed` the
940	  converse, each entry being `{"row": {...}, "count": <int>}` sorted by the
941	  canonical (key-sorted) JSON text of `row`.
942	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/snapshots/{base_snapshot_id}/diff/{target_snapshot_id}` —
943	  read-only comparison of two snapshots belonging to two **different** schema
944	  versions of the path dataset; the baseline snapshot is named first and the
945	  target second, and either version order is allowed. It takes no request
946	  body and no query parameters (`422`). Unknown dataset or snapshot → `404`,
947	  checked ahead of every request-shape check; a snapshot owned by another
948	  dataset, or two snapshots of the same schema version (same-version
949	  comparisons still go through the snapshot-id diff endpoint) → `422`. The
950	  JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace,
951	  exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `base_snapshot_id`,
952	  `base_version`, `target_snapshot_id`, `target_version`, `field_changes`,
953	  `added` and `removed` in that order. `field_changes` lists only additions,
954	  removals, type changes and nullability changes of the two versions' field
955	  definitions, reusing the compatibility/trajectory literals (`added`,
956	  `removed`, `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened`, `nullable_loosened`);
957	  several changes of one field collapse into a single entry (a type change
958	  wins over a nullability change), entries sort by field name and each entry
959	  has `field`, `kind`, `before` and `after`, with the missing side `null`
960	  (never omitted). Rows are projected onto exactly the field names defined
961	  in both versions — other stored keys and fields absent from a row do not
962	  participate — and the projections are compared with the same-version
963	  snapshot diff's multiset semantics (object key order irrelevant, array
964	  order and value types significant, duplicates counted). `added` lists
965	  rows present more often or only on the target side, `removed` the
966	  converse, each entry `{"row", "count"}` sorted by the canonical
967	  (key-sorted) JSON text of the projected row. The comparison is fully
968	  read-only: snapshots, rows, field definitions, the lineage impact cache
969	  and every privacy trail are never touched, and the result is identical
970	  across process restarts.
971	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/quality-rules/evaluate`
972	  — evaluate the version's enabled quality rules over the snapshot's persisted
973	  rows. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`);
974	  unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404` (checked first), and a snapshot
975	  owned by another version → `422`. The response and the rule semantics are
976	  exactly those of the row-submission evaluation (`{"dataset", "version",
977	  "results"}`), the snapshot and its rows are never modified, and every
978	  successful evaluation appends the same immutable history summary (with
979	  `row_count` set to the snapshot's actual row count) that also feeds the
980	  evaluation diff and anomaly detection. An empty snapshot is recorded with
981	  zero violations.
